prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We investigate the possibility of electroweak phase transition in the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) with an extra $U(1)'$. This model has two Higgs doublets and a singlet, in addition to a singlet exotic quark superfield. We find that at the one-loop level this model may accommodate the electroweak phase transitions that are strongly first-order in a reasonably large region of the parameter space. In the parameter region where the phase transitions take place, we observe that the lightest scalar Higgs boson has a smaller mass when the strength of the phase transition becomes weaker. Also, the other three heavier neutral Higgs bosons get more large masses when the strength of the phase transition becomes weaker.

outputs.L1: We investigate the possibility of an electroweak phase transition in the minimal supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) symmetry. In addition to two Higgs doublets and a singlet, the model contains a singlet exotic-quark superfield. We find that, at the one-loop level, the model can accommodate strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions over a reasonably large region of parameter space. Within the parameter region where these phase transitions occur, the mass of the lightest scalar Higgs boson decreases as the strength of the phase transition weakens. Conversely, the masses of the other three, heavier neutral Higgs bosons increase as the phase transition becomes weaker.
outputs.L2: We examine electroweak symmetry breaking in an MSSM extension containing an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. Along with two Higgs doublets and one singlet, the model includes a singlet exotic-quark superfield. Our one-loop analysis indicates that strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions can occur across a fairly broad region of parameter space. Within the region supporting such transitions, a reduction in transition strength is associated with a lower mass for the lightest scalar Higgs boson, while the remaining three heavier neutral Higgs bosons become more massive.
outputs.L3:
This study investigates electroweak phase transitions within the minimal supersymmetric standard model extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. The Higgs sector consists of two Higgs doublets and one singlet field, while the matter content also includes a singlet exotic-quark superfield.

A one-loop analysis of the finite-temperature effective potential shows that strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions can occur over a reasonably broad region of the model’s parameter space. This result suggests that the \(U(1)'\)-extended model can provide favorable conditions for mechanisms such as electroweak baryogenesis.

The strength of the phase transition is also correlated with the neutral Higgs-boson mass spectrum. As the transition becomes weaker, the mass of the lightest scalar Higgs boson decreases. In contrast, the masses of the three heavier neutral Higgs bosons increase. Thus, the character of the electroweak phase transition is closely connected to the predicted Higgs spectrum in this extended supersymmetric framework.
outputs.L4:
This study investigates the electroweak phase transition at the one-loop level in a supersymmetric extension of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model based on an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. The Higgs sector contains two electroweak doublets and a singlet field, while the matter content is enlarged by a singlet exotic-quark superfield. The extra gauge interaction, the singlet sector, and the associated supersymmetric and soft-breaking interactions modify both the zero-temperature Higgs potential and its finite-temperature behavior, providing new mechanisms for strengthening the electroweak phase transition.

The analysis is performed using the one-loop finite-temperature effective potential, including the relevant radiative and thermal contributions from the particles that couple most strongly to the Higgs fields. The critical temperature is identified as the temperature at which the symmetric and broken minima of the effective potential become degenerate. The strength of the transition is then characterized by the ratio of the electroweak order parameter at the critical temperature to the critical temperature. A value of this ratio of order unity or larger corresponds to a strongly first-order transition, as is generally required to suppress baryon-number-violating sphaleron processes in the broken phase.

A numerical exploration of the model’s parameter space shows that strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions can occur over a sizable range of couplings, soft supersymmetry-breaking parameters, vacuum expectation values, and Higgs-sector masses. The singlet and exotic-quark contributions can significantly alter the shape of the thermal potential and generate or enhance the barrier separating the symmetric and electroweak-broken phases. Consequently, the model is not restricted to a narrowly tuned region in order to realize a sufficiently strong transition.

The results also reveal a relationship between the strength of the phase transition and the neutral Higgs spectrum. Parameter choices that yield weaker transitions tend to be associated with a lighter lightest scalar Higgs boson and comparatively heavier remaining neutral Higgs states. Conversely, stronger transitions arise when the interactions and mass parameters of the extended Higgs sector produce a more favorable thermal potential and a larger separation between the competing minima.

Overall, the additional \(U(1)'\) symmetry, singlet dynamics, and exotic matter content substantially enrich the electroweak symmetry-breaking pattern relative to the MSSM. The existence of broad parameter regions supporting a strongly first-order transition makes this framework a promising setting for viable electroweak symmetry breaking and potentially for electroweak baryogenesis, while the correlations with the Higgs spectrum provide useful guidance for phenomenological and experimental tests.
outputs.L5: The Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) extends the Standard Model by introducing supersymmetric partners for known particles. Unlike the Standard Model, the MSSM requires two Higgs doublets, resulting in five physical Higgs bosons: two neutral CP-even states, one neutral CP-odd state, and two charged states. The lightest MSSM Higgs boson can resemble the Higgs particle observed at the Large Hadron Collider. This extended Higgs sector provides rich phenomenology and offers important tests of supersymmetry in current and future experiments.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper investigating strongly first-order electroweak phase transitions in the MSSM extended by an extra \(U(1)'\).
counterfactuals.output: We investigate the electroweak phase transition in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model extended by an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry. The enlarged Higgs sector, including a singlet field responsible for \(U(1)'\) breaking and generating an effective \(\mu\) term, introduces new tree-level interactions that can strengthen the electroweak phase transition without requiring exceptionally light stops. We construct the finite-temperature effective potential including one-loop Coleman–Weinberg corrections, thermal contributions, and daisy resummation, and numerically determine the critical and nucleation temperatures over phenomenologically viable regions of parameter space. We impose constraints from electroweak symmetry breaking, Higgs measurements, collider searches for additional Higgs bosons and the \(Z'\), and vacuum stability. We identify parameter regions supporting a strongly first-order transition, quantified by \(v(T_n)/T_n \gtrsim 1\), and analyze the underlying multi-field tunneling dynamics. The strongest transitions are associated with sizable singlet–doublet interactions and a tree-level barrier between the symmetric and electroweak-breaking phases. We also discuss the implications for electroweak baryogenesis and estimate the stochastic gravitational-wave signal generated by bubble nucleation and plasma motion. Our results demonstrate that \(U(1)'\)-extended supersymmetric models provide a well-motivated framework for a strong electroweak phase transition with complementary signatures at colliders and future gravitational-wave observatories.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the one-loop electroweak phase transition behavior and neutral Higgs mass spectrum in a \(U(1)'\)-extended minimal supersymmetric standard model with two Higgs doublets, a singlet, and an exotic quark superfield.
counterfactuals.output:
In the \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM, the Higgs sector contains \(H_d\), \(H_u\), and a singlet \(S\), with a superpotential term schematically
\[
W\supset \lambda S H_uH_d+h_tQH_ut^c+h_kS\,D\bar D ,
\]
where \(D,\bar D\) are exotic quark superfields required in typical anomaly-free constructions.

### One-loop electroweak phase transition

- The finite-temperature effective potential consists of the tree-level \(F\)-, \(D\)- and soft-breaking terms plus Coleman–Weinberg and thermal contributions from the top/stop, gauge, Higgs, and exotic-quark/squark sectors.
- A key feature is the soft trilinear interaction
  \[
  \lambda A_\lambda S H_uH_d+\text{h.c.},
  \]
  which can generate a barrier between the electroweak-symmetric or singlet-dominated minimum and the broken minimum already at tree level. Thus the transition need not rely solely on the relatively small thermal cubic gauge-boson terms.
- For sizable \(\lambda A_\lambda\) and suitable singlet and soft masses, the critical temperature \(T_c\) is defined by two degenerate minima, and the transition can satisfy
  \[
  \frac{v_c}{T_c}\gtrsim1,
  \qquad
  v_c=\sqrt{v_d^2(T_c)+v_u^2(T_c)},
  \]
  making electroweak baryon-number preservation possible.
- Exotic quark and squark loops alter both the zero-temperature vacuum and the thermal barrier. Their effect is parameter dependent, but sizable Yukawa coupling \(h_k\) and appreciable exotic-squark splitting can significantly strengthen or shift the transition. A strong first-order transition can occur without requiring an exceptionally light stop, unlike in the minimal MSSM.
- The transition may involve a substantial change in the singlet expectation value as well as in the doublet fields, so a multi-step or singlet-assisted thermal history is also possible.

### Neutral Higgs spectrum

After \(U(1)_Y\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)'\) breaking, two neutral Goldstone modes are absorbed by \(Z\) and \(Z'\). In a CP-conserving vacuum the physical neutral sector therefore contains

\[
3\ \text{CP-even scalars }(h_1,h_2,h_3)
\quad+\quad
1\ \text{CP-odd scalar }A .
\]

Typically:

- one state is mostly SM-like and doublet dominated;
- another is the orthogonal, heavier doublet state;
- one is predominantly singlet and is often correlated with the \(Z'\)-breaking scale;
- the physical pseudoscalar mass is controlled mainly by \(\lambda A_\lambda\), the singlet VEV, and \(\tan\beta\).

The SM-like Higgs receives the usual top/stop correction together with additional \(F\)-term, \(U(1)'\) \(D\)-term, and exotic-quark/squark corrections. Consequently its mass upper bound is higher than in the MSSM and can readily accommodate a \(125\) GeV Higgs; in favorable parameter regions one-loop estimates allow masses roughly in the \(140\)–\(160\) GeV range, though the precise limit is model and spectrum dependent. If soft parameters contain physical phases, one-loop stop and exotic-squark effects mix CP-even and CP-odd fields, producing four neutral Higgs mass eigenstates of indefinite CP rather than a \(3+1\) decomposition.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Can the MSSM with an additional \(U(1)'\) gauge symmetry support a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition? Briefly describe the relevant particle content, parameter space, and Higgs-mass correlations.
counterfactuals.output:
Yes. In a \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM (UMSSM), a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition can occur without requiring the very light stop usually invoked in the MSSM.

- **Particle content:** Besides the MSSM fields, the model contains a \(U(1)'\) gauge boson \(Z'\), its gaugino, and at least one charged singlet superfield \(S\). The superpotential includes
  \[
  W\supset \lambda S H_uH_d ,
  \]
  generating an effective \(\mu\)-term, \(\mu_{\rm eff}=\lambda\langle S\rangle\). Additional exotic matter is generally required for anomaly cancellation but may be heavy.

- **Origin of the strong transition:** The soft term
  \[
  \lambda A_\lambda S H_uH_d+\text{h.c.}
  \]
  and singlet–doublet interactions can create a barrier in the finite-temperature potential already at tree level. Strong transitions, conventionally \(v_c/T_c\gtrsim1\), are favored by moderate-to-large \(\lambda\), sizable \(A_\lambda\), low or moderate \(\tan\beta\), and appreciable singlet–doublet mixing. One- or two-step transitions are possible.

- **Parameter-space caveat:** Present \(Z'\) limits often force the singlet VEV into the multi-TeV range. In the minimal model this can decouple the singlet and make a strong transition harder, although suitable charge assignments, suppressed \(Z'\) couplings, or secluded \(U(1)'\)-breaking sectors can preserve viable regions.

- **Higgs correlations:** Extra \(F\)- and \(U(1)'\) \(D\)-terms raise the tree-level SM-like Higgs mass,
  \[
  m_h^2\sim M_Z^2\cos^22\beta+\lambda^2v^2\sin^22\beta
  +g_{1'}^2v^2\!\left(Q_{H_d}\cos^2\beta+Q_{H_u}\sin^2\beta\right)^2+\Delta_{\rm loop}.
  \]
  Thus a \(125\) GeV Higgs is compatible with less reliance on heavy stops. Strong-transition points often correlate with a relatively light singlet-dominated CP-even scalar and non-negligible Higgs mixing; the observed Higgs may be either the lightest or next-to-lightest state. Exact mass bounds are model- and collider-constraint dependent.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise physics-paper abstract about electroweak baryogenesis in a supersymmetric \(U(1)'\) extension, emphasizing one-loop results and how the phase-transition strength relates to the masses of the four neutral Higgs bosons.
counterfactuals.output: We investigate electroweak baryogenesis in a supersymmetric \(U(1)'\) extension of the Standard Model, including the full one-loop zero- and finite-temperature effective potential. The additional singlet and \(U(1)'\) interactions generate a tree-level barrier that is reinforced by radiative and thermal corrections, allowing a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition without requiring an exceptionally light stop. By scanning the Higgs-sector parameters, we correlate the order parameter \(v_c/T_c\) with the physical masses of the four neutral Higgs bosons. Strong transitions generally favor a comparatively light, doublet-like scalar, while the singlet-dominated and heavier neutral states may remain substantially heavier; nevertheless, mixing and one-loop effects prevent a simple dependence on any single mass. These results show that the transition strength is controlled by the collective neutral-Higgs spectrum and mixing structure, providing collider-testable conditions for successful electroweak baryogenesis.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the main findings of a study of electroweak phase transitions in the \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM, including whether viable transitions occur over a sizable parameter region and what happens to the lightest and heavier scalar Higgs masses as the transition weakens.
counterfactuals.output:
The study found that the \(U(1)'\)-extended MSSM can support a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition—typically characterized by \(v_c/T_c \gtrsim 1\)—over a substantial, rather than finely tuned, region of parameter space. The singlet sector and its tree-level Higgs interactions help generate the required barrier in the finite-temperature potential.

A characteristic mass trend was also observed as the transition becomes weaker:

- the lightest CP-even scalar Higgs becomes heavier;
- the heavier CP-even scalar Higgs states become lighter.

Thus, weakening the transition tends to compress the neutral scalar-Higgs spectrum, while the strongest transitions correlate with a relatively light lightest Higgs and heavier additional scalars.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
